# Physics / chemistry (class 11), ~2 minutes, written by Claude for F-014 S4 (hard topics). Expect: a content slide on
# gases; "blood pressure" and "greenhouse gases" are traps; "let me show you an ideal gas in a cylinder with a piston"
# opens simulation mode; 100 kPa, 300 K, 2 L: n 0.0802 mol; heated to 600 K at constant pressure: V 4 L (computed);
# then compressed to 1 L at constant temperature: P 400 kPa (computed); "heated to 900 K" alone asks what is held;
# an adiabatic change is a notice; back to the slides.
@setup subject="Physics" grade=11 topic="Gas laws"

Good morning. Today we study how a gas responds when we heat it or squeeze it.
[pause 1]
Your blood pressure and greenhouse gases are different topics, today we mean a gas in a container.
[pause 1.5]
Let me show you an ideal gas in a cylinder with a piston.
The gas is at 100 kPa and 300 K and occupies 2 litres.
[pause 1]
Now it is heated to 600 K at constant pressure.
The molecules move faster and push the piston up, so the volume grows.
[pause 1.5]
Next we compress it to 1 litre at constant temperature.
The molecules hit the walls more often, so the pressure goes up.
[pause 1]
Suppose the gas is heated to 900 K.
In an adiabatic change no heat flows in or out, but that comes later in thermodynamics.
[pause 1.5]
Okay, let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1]
So P V equals n R T connects pressure, volume, temperature and the amount of gas.
